subject: soc-rt-dy
title: SOC.RT.DY.------PHY.U.P.
description: Diagram in SD(SY)-25 (Spectacle-Diversion Syndrome, Level One) accompanying Braxton's opening of the hippie-movement analysis: 'the principles which manifest themselves in each spectacle-diversion sequence, and how people relate to what this sequence is supposed to mean — that clarifies the real fabric of American culture.' (C)SOC-RT-DY (the concept of social reality dynamics) is crossed with PHY-U-P (physical universe particulars): the question is what social-reality-dynamics produces when crossed with physical-universe-particulars in a culture where the diversion sequence determines self-perception. (R)TM (the reality of time) and (R)INT (the reality of interior) form an upper-right cluster. CUL-INFO-B (culture-information basis) sits centrally between subject and partner. POL-P (political particulars) feeds upward from the lower-left into the subject. CN-INFO (continuance information) and PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) form the central downward chain. TRS (transference) anchors the lower-right margin. Structural argument: social-reality-dynamics crossed with physical-universe-particulars is mediated by the culture-information-basis as a central hub, with political-particulars as the lower upstream and time-as-real plus interior-as-real as the upper output frame. The diagram exposes Braxton's structural commitment: any honest reading of social-reality requires both physical-universe-particulars and the culture-information-basis — the hippie movement (the surrounding prose context) failed precisely because it took social-reality as primary without crossing it against physical-universe ground.
